Bootstrap confidence intervals for properties of an estimated chain

Source: R/bootstrapProperties.R
bootstrapProperties.Rd

Estimates a Markov chain from one or more observed sequences and gives bootstrap standard errors and confidence intervals for properties of the chain, such as the second largest eigenvalue modulus, the spectral gap, the relaxation time or the mixing time, which the corresponding functions return as point values only.

Usage

bootstrapProperties(
  data,
  statistics = c("slem", "spectralGap", "relaxationTime", "mixingTime"),
  nboot = 1000L,
  method = c("multinomial", "parametric"),
  level = 0.95,
  type = c("percentile", "basic"),
  possibleStates = character(),
  epsilon = 0.25,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

An observed sequence (character, factor or numeric vector), a list of independent sequences, or a square matrix of transition counts with the states as row and column names (only with method = "multinomial").

statistics

Either a character vector of built-in statistics, among "slem", "spectralGap", "relaxationTime", "mixingTime" (the default four), "entropyRate", "kemenyConstant" and "steadyStates", or a named list whose elements are such names or functions of a markovchain object returning a numeric vector of fixed length (an unnamed built-in name is named after itself).

nboot

A single integer of at least 2: the number of bootstrap replicates.

method

How the replicates are drawn: "multinomial" (the default) resamples, for each state, its observed number of departures from the estimated row; "parametric" simulates new sequences of the observed lengths from the estimated chain, each starting from the observed first state. See Details.

level

The confidence level, a single number in \((0, 1)\).

type

The kind of interval: "percentile" (the default) or "basic".

possibleStates

Optional character vector of states to include even if they are not observed. Every state must be left at least once in the data, otherwise its transition probabilities cannot be estimated.

epsilon

The total variation threshold of mixingTime.

seed

An optional whole number. When given, the replicates are drawn after set.seed(seed) and the caller's random number stream is left untouched.

Value

An object of class "markovchainBootstrap", a list with:

estimate

The statistics of the estimated chain.

ci

A matrix with one row per statistic and the lower and upper limits of the interval.

se, bias

Bootstrap standard errors and bias estimates (mean of the replicates minus the estimate).

failures

For each statistic, the number of replicates for which it could not be computed (they are left out of the intervals).

replicates

The nboot by statistics matrix of bootstrap values.

chain

The estimated markovchain.

counts

The matrix of observed transition counts.

method, type, level, nboot

The settings used.

Details

The chain is estimated by maximum likelihood, \(\hat P_{ij} = n_{ij}/n_i\). With method = "multinomial" a replicate draws, for every state \(i\), the counts \((n^*_{i1}, \ldots, n^*_{ir})\) from a multinomial distribution with \(n_i\) trials and probabilities \(\hat P_{i\cdot}\), and re-estimates \(P^*_{ij} = n^*_{ij}/n_i\). This is the conditional bootstrap of Basawa et al. (1990), valid for finite ergodic chains, which keeps the number of visits to each state fixed. With method = "parametric" a replicate simulates a new path of each observed length from \(\hat P\), as in Kulperger and Prakasa Rao (1989); the numbers of visits then vary too, and a replicate in which some state is never left cannot be estimated and counts as a failure. The parametric version is slower but closer to the actual sampling scheme of a single path.

When all the statistics are among "slem", "spectralGap", "relaxationTime" and "mixingTime", the replicates are computed in C++, with one eigen-decomposition per replicate; otherwise each replicate is turned into a markovchain object and the statistics are evaluated in R. The results are the same either way, and the random draws come from R's generator, so set.seed and seed control them.

The percentile interval is formed by the \((1-\code{level})/2\) and \((1+\code{level})/2\) quantiles of the replicates; the basic interval reflects them around the estimate, \(2\hat\theta - q_{1-\alpha/2}\) and \(2\hat\theta - q_{\alpha/2}\).

Some care is needed in reading the results. The SLEM and the spectral gap are not smooth functions of the matrix where the second largest eigenvalue modulus is reached by more than one eigenvalue, the mixing time is an integer, and replicates of a chain with rare transitions may be reducible or periodic, in which case some statistics fail; the bootstrap distribution of all of them can be skewed. The intervals are therefore approximate, and their coverage should be checked by simulation for the case at hand, as done in the package's vignette. The asymptotic theory of these estimators is developed by Hsu et al. (2019) for the spectral gap of reversible chains.

References

Basawa, I. V., Green, T. A., McCormick, W. P. and Taylor, R. L. (1990). Asymptotic bootstrap validity for finite Markov chains. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 19(4), 1493-1510.

Kulperger, R. J. and Prakasa Rao, B. L. S. (1989). Bootstrapping a finite state Markov chain. Sankhya, Series A, 51(2), 178-191.

Hsu, D., Kontorovich, A., Levin, D. A., Peres, Y., Szepesvari, C. and Wolfer, G. (2019). Mixing time estimation in reversible Markov chains from a single sample path. The Annals of Applied Probability, 29(4), 2439-2480. doi:10.1214/18-AAP1457

See also

slem, spectralGap, relaxationTime, mixingTime, markovchainFit (whose method = "bootstrap" gives bootstrap standard errors of the transition probabilities themselves)

Examples

data(rain)
set.seed(1)
boot <- bootstrapProperties(rain$rain, nboot = 200)
boot
#> Bootstrap of a Markov chain on 3 states (multinomial, 200 replicates)
#> 
#>                estimate      se   2.5%  97.5%
#> slem             0.4106 0.03039 0.3501 0.4710
#> spectralGap      0.5894 0.03039 0.5290 0.6499
#> relaxationTime   1.6970 0.08766 1.5390 1.8910
#> mixingTime       2.0000 0.12190 2.0000 2.0000
#> 
#> Percentile 95% intervals.
boot$ci
#>                     2.5%     97.5%
#> slem           0.3501461 0.4710463
#> spectralGap    0.5289537 0.6498539
#> relaxationTime 1.5388076 1.8905255
#> mixingTime     2.0000000 2.0000000

# any function of the chain, here the stationary probability of no rain
bootstrapProperties(rain$rain, nboot = 200, seed = 2,
  statistics = list(dry = function(mc) steadyStates(mc)[1, "0"]))
#> Bootstrap of a Markov chain on 3 states (multinomial, 200 replicates)
#> 
#>     estimate      se   2.5%  97.5%
#> dry   0.5009 0.02326 0.4528 0.5445
#> 
#> Percentile 95% intervals.
